timing: Editorial cue timings retained from the original animation; English narration is a translation and is not aligned to a recorded voice.

pointing_event.note: Logical image distances, not metres or a calibrated detector response

timing_event.saved_times: illustrative relative nanoseconds; not real IceCube data

cues.narration: One reason for building a detector array spanning a cubic kilometer is to determine where a neutrino came from.
cues.visual: A three-dimensional array appears without an enclosing cube; a muon neutrino approaches an interaction point.

cues.narration: If a muon neutrino interacts in the ice and produces a muon, the muon travels in nearly the same direction at high energies.
cues.visual: A muon emerges at a small angle to the incoming neutrino; nearby DOMs light up.

cues.narration: Reconstructing the muon's track can therefore reveal the neutrino's arrival direction with high precision.
cues.visual: The track extends backward to emphasize the arrival direction, followed by a close-up of a hit DOM.

cues.narration: IceCube's Digital Optical Modules, or DOMs, have nanosecond timing precision: a billionth of a second.
cues.visual: A large 0.000000001 s appears below 1 ns = 10⁻⁹ s, with eight decimal zeros appearing in sequence.
Two strings with three DOMs each appear; all six clocks share the same phase.

cues.narration: When a DOM detects Cherenkov light, it measures and records the signal.
cues.visual: One muon passes between the strings; a timestamp is recorded when its trailing cone reaches the first DOM.

cues.narration: Comparing which detectors received light, and when, allows us to reconstruct the particle's path.
cues.visual: The same muon and cone produce six fixed timestamps; the reconstructed track then becomes prominent.

cues.narration: The entire detector array is embedded deep in the ice.
cues.visual: The DOMs return to the full array as the camera pulls back to show the surface and depth.

cues.narration: The ice blocks surface light and filters out many unwanted particles produced by cosmic rays.
cues.visual: Daylight fades near the surface; most shower particles stop above the array, while a few penetrating muons remain.

cues.narration: The deep ice is also exceptionally transparent.
cues.visual: The camera returns to the deep array and enlarges a DOM to introduce light propagation.

cues.narration: Cherenkov light can travel tens or even hundreds of meters to reach detectors.
cues.visual: Schematic light pulses reach widely separated DOMs.

cues.narration: But the ice is not perfectly transparent.
cues.visual: Two additional optical paths appear beside the direct path.

cues.narration: Some light is absorbed, and some is scattered into new directions.
cues.visual: One pulse fades away; another changes direction several times and arrives later.

cues.narration: To measure these effects, each DOM contains 12 LED flashers.
cues.visual: A receiving DOM enlarges to reveal a schematic flasher board with 12 LEDs.

cues.narration: They emit controlled light pulses that nearby DOMs detect, revealing how light travels through the ice.
cues.visual: The DOM becomes a transmitter; surrounding DOMs record repeated controlled pulses.

cues.narration: This calibrates both the optical properties of the ice and the timing response of the detectors.
cues.visual: Direct and scattered paths remain visible alongside measured pulse-time points and a fitted response curve.
